title: Terraria happiness: biome/neighbour love-hate, crowding, solitude, Princess, happiness dialogue
player_outcome: Prices follow Terraria's happiness rules: loved biomes and neighbours give discounts, a crowded town costs more, living alone is a bonus, and the Princess makes everyone happier. A 'Happiness' button in each NPC's chat explains how they feel ('I love living in the Forest!', 'It's too crowded here.').
design: Verified: TownCommerce.Mood/PriceFactor (TownCommerce.cs:77-99) is a linear score with a 25 m radius and no solitude or Princess factor.

New Gameplay/Town/TownHappiness.cs: Evaluate(TownNpc npc) → HappinessReport(float Factor, List<HappinessReason> Reasons). Multipliers from TownConfig.Happiness: love 0.88, like 0.94, dislike 1.06, hate 1.12 (scores ±2/±1). Biome at home, layer at home (new MoodEntry.Layer, for Underground), neighbours within NearRadius (12.5 m = 25 tiles) and far counts within FarRadius (60 m). Crowded: +0.05 for each near neighbour over 3. Solitude: ≤2 near and ≤4 far gives 0.95. Princess (TownNpcDef.LovedByAll) nearby counts as loved. Homeless adds a penalty. Clamp to Min/MaxPriceFactor. Non-resident kinds get factor 1.
TownCommerce.PriceFactor delegates to TownHappiness; keep Mood(npc, out n) as a thin wrapper for existing tests or update them.

Dialogue: TownConfig.HappinessLines templates per reason key (loveBiome 'I love living in the {biome}!', hateNeighbor 'I can't stand being near {neighbor}.', crowded, solitude, homeless 'I need a place to call home.', princess 'The Princess brightens my day.', content 'I'm content.'). TownNpcDef.HappinessLines holds optional per-NPC overrides. TownHappiness.Describe(report) → string.
TownDialog: a 'Happiness' button for housed residents (through the P5-13 service registry as the implicit 'happiness' entry).

Data: rewrite every NPC's mood array from Terraria 1.4's happiness table (biome mapping: Forest→forest, Underground→layer underground/cavern, Desert→desert, Snow→tundra, Jungle→jungle, Ocean→ocean, Hallow→hallow, Mushroom→mushroom). Princess gets lovedByAll: true.
files_modify: src/Strata.Core/Commands/TownCommands.cs — the 'town' listing shows factor and reasons
data_changes: all 29 mood arrays re-authored from the Terraria happiness table; town.json happiness config
tests: TownHappinessTests: a loved biome gives factor ≈0.88; a hated neighbour 1.12; 5 near neighbours ≈1.10; solitude 0.95; the Princess neighbour lowers the factor; clamping; Describe includes the biome line
TownTests.PriceFactor tests (TownTests.cs:134-137) updated to the new expectations
verification: In game: the 'town' console lists factors; the Happiness button text matches the NPC's situation
risks: Terraria's exact solitude and crowding numbers need verifying on the wiki (Happiness page), and pylons are out of scope.
The 3D radius over-counts stacked houses; use a horizontal distance with a vertical cap (config).
